title: C. elegans Dissociation for FACS and RNA-seq
author: Robert TP Williams
materials: Prepare reagents in advance L15-10 Buffer: Mix 500 ml Leibovitz's L-15 Medium, 50 ml Fetal Bovine Serum (heat inactivated), 50 ul of 100x Penicillin-Streptomycin solution and 7.7 g sucrose. Filter with 0.2 micron pore filter. Store at 4ºC. Egg Buffer: Mix 29.5 ml of 2M NaCl, 12 ml of 2M KCl, 1 ml of 1M CaCl2, 1 ml of MgCl2, 12.5 ml of 1M HEPES-NaOH pH 7.2 and 435 ml molecular grade water. Filter with 0.2 micron pore filter. Store at 4ºC. Pronase E solution (15 mg/ml): Weigh 150 mg of Protease from Streptomyces griseus (Sigma P8811-1G) into a 15 ml tube. Dissolve the enzyme in 10 ml of Egg Buffer. Nutate the solution for approximately 10 minutes until dissolved. Prepare 1 ml aliquots in 1.5 ml tubes. Store aliquots at -20ºC. SDS-DTT solution: To ensure treatment efficacy, the SDS-DTT solution is prepared fresh on the day of the experiment. Additionally, several aliquots of DTT powder in 1.5 ml tubes are prepared in advance and stored at -20ºC. To prepare the SDS-DTT solution, first resuspend 154 mg of DTT powder with 1 mL of Egg Buffer on the day of the experiment. Then, combine the following reagents in a 15 ml tube (final concentrations in parenthesis): 100 uL of 1M HEPES pH8 (20 mM), 125 uL of 10% SDS (0.25%), 1 mL of 1M DTT (200 mM), 250 uL of 60% sucrose (3%), and 3.525 mL of molecular grade water for a final volume of 5 mL. The SDS-DTT solution is one of the most important reagents to ensure successful dissociation of post-embryonic worms. To check that the SDS-DTT solution is working properly, incubate worms in freshly prepared SDS-DTT solution under a dissection microscope. When prepared properly, worms should dissolve within ~10 minutes of observation.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the workspace and materials required for the dissociation process.

substeps.instruction: Cool swinging bucket centrifuge to 4ºC.
Thaw pronase aliquots at room temperature.
Place L15-10 and egg buffer on ice.
Wash and sterilize dounce homogenizer and pestle A using 1ml H2O and 1ml 70% EtOH.

steps.title: Harvest and wash L1 worms
steps.instruction: Collect synchronized L1 worms and remove contaminating E. coli.

substeps.instruction: Harvest synchronized L1 worms by washing plates with fresh M9.
Pass the harvested L1 suspension through a 20 micron filter to remove debris and dead embryos.
Pellet worms in a 15 ml tube for 1 min at 2,000 rcf.
Discard supernatant and repeat M9 washes until the supernatant is free of visible E. coli.

steps.title: Prepare worm pellet for dissociation
steps.instruction: Concentrate the worms and aliquot a sample for RNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge worm suspension at 2,000 rcf for 1 minute.
Resuspend the worm pellet in 1 ml of M9 and transfer to a 1.5 ml tube.
Pellet the worms again at 2,000 rcf for 1 minute.
Transfer 10 ul of L1 worm pellet to 1ml of Qiazol and store at -80°C for downstream RNA analysis.

steps.title: Digest cuticle with SDS-DTT
steps.instruction: Treat worms with SDS-DTT to digest the cuticle, ensuring the incubation time does not exceed 2 minutes to avoid sample damage.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the worm pellet in 200 ul of fresh SDS-DTT solution (if L1 pellet exceeds 200 ul, utilize 2x the L1 pellet volume).
Incubate for 2 min at room temperature; worms should look ruffled and pharynx should change from thin/elongated to short/round.
Quench reaction by adding 800 ul of ice cold egg buffer.
Pellet worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4ºC.
Decant supernatant and replace with 1 ml of ice-cold egg buffer.
Repeat the egg buffer wash for a total of 5 washes.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion and homogenization
steps.instruction: Use Pronase E and mechanical force to dissociate the worms into a cell slurry.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend SDS-DTT treated worms in 200 ul of 15 mg/ml Pronase E.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature while nutating.
Transfer the worm suspension to a 2 ml glass dounce homogenizer.
Perform 100 strokes with dounce pestle A to generate a worm slurry.
Visually confirm worm dissociation by viewing a 2 ul sample of worm slurry on a fluorescent microscope.

steps.title: Separate dissociated cells from intact worms
steps.instruction: Use low-speed centrifugation to isolate cells in the supernatant from intact worms in the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Pellet undissociated worms at 100 rcf for 1 minute at 4ºC in a swinging bucket centrifuge.
Visually confirm fluorescent cells are present in the supernatant and not in the pellet (adjust speed/time if cells are found in the pellet).

steps.title: Quantify and verify cell yield
steps.instruction: Count the cells and adjust concentration if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 ul of cell suspension to a Bio-Rad TC20 automated cell counting slide or a hemocytometer.
Microscopically confirm fluorescent cells are present.
If concentration is above 1 x 10^6 cells/ml, dilute the sample to 1 x 10^6 cells/ml using L15-10.
Note: Expected yield is 2 x 10^6 to 4 x 10^6 total cells. If yield is < 1 x 10^6 cells and intact worms remain, repeat SDS-DTT, Pronase E, and dounce homogenization steps.

steps.title: Quench and wash cells
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction and wash the cells with L15-10.

substeps.instruction: Quench the Pronase E treatment by adding 1 ml of L15-10.
Pellet the worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the worms in 1 ml of L15-10.
Pellet the worms at 13,000 rcf for 15 seconds at 4°C.
Resuspend the worms in 1ml of L15-10.

steps.title: Final cell harvest and filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension and aliquot for RNA-seq or FACS.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 1 ml of the cell-containing supernatant, keeping the pipette away from pelleted worm debris.
Dispense the cell suspension through a 35-micron nylon mesh filter into a 5 ml flow cytometry tube.
Resuspend remaining worm slurry in 1ml of L15-10.
Transfer 70 ul of cells to 1 ml of Qiazol and store at -80°C for downstream RNA analysis.
Retain the remaining ~2ml of cells for FACS.

steps.title: Iterative dissociation for sorting strain
steps.instruction: For the sorting strain, repeat the dissociation and harvest process to maximize yield.

substeps.instruction: Perform additional rounds of dissociation and cell harvest (repeating the steps from Pronase E treatment through filtration).
Perform a total of two to three homogenization cycles until few intact worms remain.
Final total cell suspension volumes should be 1ml for control strain and 2-3ml for sorting strain.
